playbook.notes: Mutant Menace (The Wise Mothman, BUG counters and rad/mill). Written from 12 stock goldfish games (seeds 23001-23012): stock kills on turn 11.3, casts Mothman on own turn 4 to 11 (median 5), never cast Bloatfly Swarm, Raul, Feral Ghoul, Struggle for Project Purity, Guardian Project or Contaminated Drink, and under-cast its ramp (Cultivate 1 of 5, Talisman of Dominance 1 of 5) and the counter doublers (Winding Constrictor, Hardened Scales held with the mana up). Rule 1: ramp first. Rule 2: the commander as soon as it can be cast (each mill of a nonland card of ours then grows the team). Rule 3: the counter doublers next, before the creatures they multiply. Rule 4: the engines (Raul, Hancock, Guardian Project, Inexorable Tide, Marcus, Scorchbeast, Mirelurk Queen). Rule 5: tap Raul in the first main phase so every player mills one before combat (Mothman, Mirelurk and Scorchbeast trigger on our own nonland mills), library 30 or more. Rule 6: the rest of the creatures, dearest first, whatever Forge thinks of them (Bloatfly Swarm was never cast by stock). Rule 7: Vault 87 and Struggle for Project Purity with 45 cards or more in the library (both draw). Rule 8: Biomass Mutation (AI:RemoveDeck:All) before combat at X 6 or more with three attackers. Rule 9: Contaminated Drink at X 3 or more with a short hand and a deep library. Rule 10: Harmonize. Rules 11-12: Strength Bobblehead's counters and Contagion Clasp's proliferate as after-combat mana sinks. Triggers: Scorchbeast's tokens and Radroach's return always; Tato Farmer's two rad counters on us only while Mothman or Scorchbeast turns our own mills into counters or tokens, with 50 cards left and 20 life. Answers (Putrefy, Atomize, Casualties of War, Nuclear Fallout, Find // Finality, Alpha Deathclaw's monstrosity, Rampaging Yao Guai, Mutational Advantage) are left to Forge for a second pass. || Version 2 (answers, written from the 200 tables of bots of ab-run #27, seed 20261260: the candidate won 55, stock 46). At the seat's losses the biggest opposing board held 12.5 creatures on average against our 3.8 (131 of 145 losses: more than ours; 111: six or more), and the seat died within a turn cycle from 19 life; Nuclear Fallout was in hand at 37 losses and cast in none of 52 games (stock: 0 of 45; Forge never casts it), Find // Finality 0 of 41. New rules 1-3, above everything, first main phase: Nuclear Fallout at X 3 (each creature -6/-6) when the strongest opposing board has more power than ours and four or more creatures; Nuclear Fallout at X 2 (-4/-4, kills tokens, spares our creatures with counters) when one opponent has six or more creatures and more than we do; Find // Finality on the same terms (Finality; whether the split card's Find half is taken instead is Forge's ordering, checked at the local tables). Rule 7 (after ramp, commander, doublers): Casualties of War, Alpha Deathclaw, Atomize when an opponent has a creature; targets and modes are Forge's (Casualties is cast only when Forge's logic agrees; Deathclaw is a plain creature cast and its enters trigger is aimed by Forge). Stock cast Deathclaw in 41 of 48 games and Casualties in 32 of 37; the engine rules starved both (10 of 51, 17 of 30). Rule 8: Vault 87 out of the old rule 7, with library 30 (was 45) and an opposing creature (chapter I steals a non-Mutant creature; chapter III draws by the greatest Mutant power). Rule 11: The Master's tap after Raul's mill in the first main phase (Forge aims it at a creature card milled this turn). Rule 12: Rampaging Yao Guai at X max, at least 3 (its artifact/enchantment destruction is Forge's choice). Rule 13 (the old rule 6) now names every creature and permanent the base left to Forge, which the play rules starved of mana: Lumbering Megasloth first (castable only when its counter discount makes it cheap), Nightkin Ambusher, The Master, Harold and Bob, Fraying Sanity, Power Fist. Stock cast them in 82 to 98% of the games drawn; the base in 17 to 60%. Rule 14: Struggle for Project Purity alone with library 45, as before. Rule 16: Mutational Advantage before combat with four attackers and three opposing creatures (our creatures with counters cannot be killed in that combat; then proliferate): the format cannot hold it for a wipe on another player's turn, and in hand it was cast in 1 of 38 games and held at 28 losses. Alpha Deathclaw's monstrosity is left to Forge: an activate rule cannot tell that the creature is already monstrous and would pay seven mana a turn for nothing. Local check, 8 tables of bots (seed 20263120): Nuclear Fallout cast by rule 1 twice (10 opposing permanents and none of ours left the battlefield; 8 opposing and 1 of ours); Finality cast once by rule 3 and countered (Swan Song); Find cast once by Forge's own choice; Alpha Deathclaw's enters trigger destroyed Doomwake Giant; Casualties took a creature, an enchantment and a land. Atomize was drawn once, in a game short of green, and is unverified: stock Forge cast it in 0 of 38 games, so Forge's logic may decline it under rule 7 too. Rule 16 (Mutational Advantage) never had four attackers. Shipped as version 2 on 2026-11-14 from ab-run #36: at 200 tables of bots (seed 20261310, opponents drawn from bots-v2 under their playbooks of 2026-11-13) 68 wins against its stock pilot's 51 (+8.5 points, 95% +1 to +16, exact test 0.050) with the attack left to Forge, the better of the two attacks on these tables (the same rules won 55 with the go-wide attack). What it casts in a share of games 15 points or more below its stock pilot on the same tables, 10 cards: Vault 12: The Necropolis (22 of 53 games drawn against 40 of 49), Agent Frank Horrigan (21 of 43 games drawn against 34 of 40), Fraying Sanity (28 of 40 games drawn against 36 of 37), Lumbering Megasloth (22 of 31 games drawn against 32 of 34), Harmonize (7 of 33 games drawn against 15 of 36), Nuka-Nuke Launcher (29 of 36 games drawn against 35 of 35), Tato Farmer (24 of 41 games drawn against 27 of 35), Strong, the Brutish Thespian (25 of 42 games drawn against 27 of 35) and 2 more. It casts 14 cards that much more often (demo-data/playtest/2026-11-14/second-pass/mutant-menace-forgeattack-card-diff.txt). VERSION 3 (2026-11-15). Version 3 = version 2 with Atomize taken out of the rule it shared with Casualties of War and Alpha Deathclaw (which left its aiming to Forge, and Forge never cast it: 0 of the 36 games it was drawn at the owner's table in ab-run #42, in hand at 23 losses; 0 of 42 under the stock pilot) and given a rule of its own right after: aimed at an opponent's nonland permanent worth four or more, the best one of the opponent that looks most dangerous (harness 0.3.4: aim). Nothing else is changed. Shipped as version 3 on 2026-11-15 from ab-run #43 (seed 20261360, the owner's table, opponents under their shipped playbooks): 43 wins of 200 against version 2's 42 on the same tables (+0.5 points, 95% -2 to +3, exact test 1.0); Atomize cast in 26 of the 30 games it was drawn (0 of 30 under version 2); its 26 casts went at the opponent that looked most dangerous 24 times and at the next one that had something worth four twice; 6 of them hit a commander and none fizzled. The rule it was read by was fixed before the run: level with or ahead of the shipped arm, and the newly named card cast in a quarter or more of the games it is drawn. VERSION 4 (2026-11-21), the candidate `v4`: version 3 with what passed its exam, part by part. RULES: the cast rules of the candidate `finisher` (rule 7 and rule 23 of this file). HOOKS: after Forge's own attack has been declared, the attackers sent at a player are sent at the opponent that looks most dangerous instead, when that opponent is ahead of the one attacked by five or more and the attack is no worse there: the damage sure to get through whatever is blocked is at least what it was, no more creatures there could block the attackers, and no attacker meets a blocker that would destroy it unless it met one where it was sent (`"aim": "danger"`; an attack that is sure to kill its target stays, and which creatures attack is not changed); and then the creatures that stayed home attack an opponent that has no creature that can block, the most dangerous such opponent first: those that deal damage, have no ability that taps them (or have vigilance) and are not wanted home by Forge's own judgement of the seat's defence (`"open": true`; a weaker opponent is not killed this way while a more dangerous one lives); and then a sure kill is taken from the most dangerous opponent down (`"finish": "leader"`: enough attackers are put on the opponent that looks most dangerous that the damage reaches its life whatever it blocks, then on the next one, and no weaker opponent is killed while a more dangerous one lives); a triggered ability of the seat that removes one permanent of an opponent (destroys it, exiles it, returns it to hand or library) is aimed at the opponent that looks most dangerous, when that opponent looks more dangerous than the one Forge aimed at by five or more and has a permanent of the same kind worth at least as much as Forge's choice or at least 4 (`"targets": {"triggers": "danger"}`); when Forge's blocks leave at least the seat's life in damage unblocked and blocks exist that would not, blocks are added, the least valuable free creatures in front of the heaviest unblocked attackers and only as many as it takes for the seat to live (`"block": {"survive": true}`). FROM THE CANDIDATE `finisher` (its rule numbers are those of its own file, playbook/variants/mutant-menace-finisher.json): WHY: Biomass Mutation (X and two: creatures you control have base power and toughness X/X until end of turn; Forge's AI is told never to play it) is the deck's finisher, on top of its +1/+1 counters. Version 3's rule casts it before the attack, for X 6 or more with three attackers, below every other play: 4 casts in the 59 games it was drawn in ab-run #45's shipped arm, in hand at 37 losses. A person casts it after blocks, when it is known who got through. RULE 7 (`keep`, harness 0.4.8), below the wipes, the mana, the commander and the four counter engines and above everything else: with the card in hand, three creatures able to attack, seven mana, and our creatures' power at least that of the strongest opposing board, the first main phase ends with the mana unspent; the rules below are read in the second main phase. RULE 23, in the seat's own declare-blockers step: Biomass Mutation for all the mana, X 4 at least, when two attackers or more are unblocked. Version 3's main-phase rule for the card stays and no longer fires when rule 7 does. WHY NOT THE FIRST TRY: the candidate `mutation` (ab-run #52) has the keep rule above everything, so that on a turn it fires the deck casts nothing before combat, not its commander and not Nuclear Fallout, whose rules are for the first main phase only; that order was written without the deck's other rules in view. With the rule here and the condition on power, the same eight replayed tables keep the mana on 10 turns where the first try kept it on 16, and cast the card after blocks as often. LOCAL CHECK: the eight tables of ab-run #45 on which the seat held the card with seven lands and three creatures on the most own turns, replayed from their seed with this file: the mana kept on 10 turns, the card cast after blocks in three games (12, 24 and 58 combat damage on those turns under the first try, which played them the same way; a player dead on two); four of the eight won against three in the baseline; by first difference three won by both, one won only by this file, three lost by both, one table untouched. SHIPPED 2026-11-21 as version 4. Every part passed its own exam beside version 3 on the same 200 tables at the owner's table (ab-run #46 to #55, seed 20261390; demo-data/ab/2026-11-21-ab-v25/, DESIGN.md section 35): wins of 200 where version 3 won 40: leader 41, aim 40, block 39, swing 43, open 44, finisher 40. No two parts were played together; the version is at the tables beside version 3 in ab-run #57 (seed 20261410). VERSION 5 CANDIDATE `guard` (2026-11-21). Version 4 with one change: after Forge's own attack has been declared and the hooks the version already has have acted, attackers are taken back when the attack leaves the seat where the opponents one after another are sure to kill it before its next turn and keeping them home prevents that, or, when nothing kept home does, where one opponent alone is (`"guard": "table"`; a sure kill's attackers stay, and an attack stands when nothing kept home would save the seat). No cast or trigger rule is changed. SHIPPED 2026-11-22 as version 5: the guard arm of ab-run #57 (seed 20261410, tables that chose nothing; demo-data/ab/2026-11-22-ab-v26/, DESIGN.md section 36). On the same 200 tables at the owner's table, every other seat a version of 2026-11-21: version 3 38 wins, version 4 46 (23 tables against 15, exact test 0.26), version 5 42 (3 against 7 beside version 4, exact test 0.34); deaths with its own creatures tapped 27 under version 4, 27 under version 5. The parts of version 4 were played together here for the first time, and over the ten decks they stand (186 tables against 155, exact test 0.10). CANDIDATE react (harness 0.4.12, docs/agents/add_react.py): version 5 with Putrefy, Atomize kept from Forge's AI and played by rules on other players' turns: at a creature attacking the seat when the attack ends its game through its best blocks and one removal changes that, or when one removal takes 6 damage or more away; otherwise in the end step before the seat's own turn at the most dangerous opponent's best permanent worth 3 or more that the spell can hit. From 3 lands the mana for one of them is kept through the seat's own turn while it has such a target. SHIPPED 2026-11-22 as version 6: the `react` arm of ab-run #64 (seed 20261460, tables that chose nothing; demo-data/ab/2026-11-22-ab-v32/, DESIGN.md section 40). Beside version 5 on the same 200 tables at the owner's table: 48 wins against 48 (10 tables against 10, exact test 1.00); Putrefy and Atomize cast in 84 of 93 card-games held (version 5: 87 of 97), 84 of the 84 casts on another player's turn (version 5: 0 of 87), 8 at an attacker. Read over the ten decks together by the rule fixed before the run: 123 tables against 117, the cards still played and the rules acting.
